verses.zh: 耶和华的膀臂并非缩短，不能拯救，耳朵并非发沉，不能听见，
verses.en: Look, the Lord’s hand is not too weak[NOTE:1] to deliver you;his ear is not too deaf to hear you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “short” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “or his ear too heavy [i.e., “dull”] to hear.”

verses.zh: 但你们的罪孽使你们与　神隔绝；你们的罪恶使他掩面不听你们。
verses.en: But your sinful acts have alienated you from your God;your sins have caused him to reject you and not listen to your prayers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and your sins have caused [his] face to be hidden from you so as not to hear.”

verses.zh: 因你们的手被血沾染，你们的指头被罪孽沾污，你们的嘴唇说谎言，你们的舌头出恶语。
verses.en: For your hands are stained with bloodand your fingers with sin;your lips speak lies,your tongue utters malicious words.

verses.zh: 无一人按公义告状，无一人凭诚实辩白；都倚靠虚妄，说谎言。所怀的是毒害；所生的是罪孽。
verses.en: No one is concerned about justice;[NOTE:1] no one sets forth his case truthfully.They depend on false words[NOTE:2] and tell lies;they conceive of oppression[NOTE:3] and give birth to sin.
notes: Heb “no one pleads with justice.”
Heb “nothing”; NAB “emptiness.”
Or “trouble” (NIV), or “harm.”

verses.zh: 他们菢毒蛇蛋，结蜘蛛网；人吃这蛋必死。这蛋被踏，必出蝮蛇。
verses.en: They hatch the eggs of a poisonous snakeand spin a spider’s web.Whoever eats their eggs will die,a poisonous snake is hatched.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “that which is pressed in hatches [as] a snake.”

verses.zh: 所结的网不能成为衣服；所做的也不能遮盖自己。他们的行为都是罪孽；手所做的都是强暴。
verses.en: Their webs cannot be used for clothing;they cannot cover themselves with what they make.Their deeds are sinful;they commit violent crimes.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “their deeds are deeds of sin, and the work of violence [is] in their hands.”

verses.zh: 他们的脚奔跑行恶；他们急速流无辜人的血；意念都是罪孽，所经过的路都荒凉毁灭。
verses.en: They are eager to do evil,[NOTE:1] quick to shed innocent blood.[NOTE:2] Their thoughts are sinful;they crush and destroy.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “their feet run to evil.”
Heb “they quickly pour out innocent blood.”
Heb “their thoughts are thoughts of sin, destruction and crushing [are] in their roadways.”

verses.zh: 平安的路，他们不知道；所行的事没有公平。他们为自己修弯曲的路；凡行此路的都不知道平安。
verses.en: They are unfamiliar with peace;their deeds are unjust.[NOTE:1] They use deceitful methods,and whoever deals with them is unfamiliar with peace.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their pathways.”
Heb “their paths they make crooked; everyone who walks in it does not know peace.”

verses.zh: 因此，公平离我们远，公义追不上我们。我们指望光亮，却是黑暗，指望光明，却行幽暗。
verses.en: For this reason deliverance[NOTE:1] is far from us[NOTE:2] and salvation does not reach us.We wait for light,[NOTE:3] but see only darkness;[NOTE:4] we wait for[NOTE:5] a bright light,[NOTE:6] but live[NOTE:7] in deep darkness.[NOTE:8]
notes: מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat), which refers to “justice” in the earlier verses, here refers to “justice from God,” or “vindication.” Because the people are unjust, God refuses to vindicate them before their enemies. See v. 11.
The prophet speaks on behalf of the sinful nation and confesses its sins.
Light here symbolizes prosperity and blessing.
Heb “but, look, darkness”; NIV “but all is darkness.”
The words “we wait for” are supplied in the translation; the verb is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
The plural noun form may indicate degree here.
Or “walk about”; NCV “all we have is darkness.”
The plural noun form may indicate degree here.

verses.zh: 我们摸索墙壁，好像瞎子；我们摸索，如同无目之人。我们晌午绊脚，如在黄昏一样；我们在肥壮人中，像死人一般。
verses.en: We grope along the wall like the blind,we grope like those who cannot see;[NOTE:1] we stumble at noontime as if it were evening.Though others are strong, we are like dead men.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like there are no eyes.”
Heb among the strong, like dead men.”

verses.zh: 我们咆哮如熊，哀鸣如鸽；指望公平，却是没有；指望救恩，却远离我们。
verses.en: We all growl like bears,we coo mournfully like doves;we wait for deliverance,[NOTE:1] but there is none,for salvation, but it is far from us.
notes: See the note at v. 9.

verses.zh: 我们的过犯在你面前增多，罪恶作见证告我们；过犯与我们同在。至于我们的罪孽，我们都知道：
verses.en: For you are aware of our many rebellious deeds,[NOTE:1] and our sins testify against us;indeed, we are aware of our rebellious deeds;we know our sins all too well.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for many are our rebellious deeds before you.”
Heb “indeed [or “for”] our rebellious deeds (are) with us, and our sins, we know them.”

verses.zh: 就是悖逆、不认识耶和华，转去不跟从我们的　神，说欺压和叛逆的话，心怀谎言，随即说出。
verses.en: We have rebelled and tried to deceive the Lord;we turned back from following our God.We stir up[NOTE:1] oppression and rebellion;we tell lies we concocted in our minds.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “speaking.” A new sentence was started here in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.”

verses.zh: 并且公平转而退后，公义站在远处；诚实在街上仆倒，正直也不得进入。
verses.en: Justice is driven back;godliness[NOTE:1] stands far off.Indeed,[NOTE:2] honesty stumbles in the city squareand morality is not even able to enter.
notes: Or “righteousness” (ASV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); KJV, NAB “justice.”
Or “for” (KJV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 诚实少见；离恶的人反成掠物。那时，耶和华看见没有公平，甚不喜悦。
verses.en: Honesty has disappeared;the one who tries to avoid evil is robbed.The Lord watches and is displeased,[NOTE:1] for there is no justice.
notes: Heb “and it is displeasing in his eyes.”

verses.zh: 他见无人拯救，无人代求，甚为诧异，就用自己的膀臂施行拯救，以公义扶持自己。
verses.en: He sees there is no advocate;[NOTE:1] he is shocked[NOTE:2] that no one intervenes.So he takes matters into his own hands;[NOTE:3] his desire for justice drives him on.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “man” (so KJV, ASV); TEV “no one to help.”
Or “appalled” (NAB, NIV, NRSV), or “disgusted.”
Heb “and his arm delivers for him.”
Heb “and his justice [or “righteousness”] supports him.”

verses.zh: 他以公义为铠甲（或译：护心镜），以拯救为头盔，以报仇为衣服，以热心为外袍。
verses.en: He wears his desire for justice[NOTE:1] like body armor,[NOTE:2] and his desire to deliver is like a helmet on his head.[NOTE:3] He puts on the garments of vengeance[NOTE:4] and wears zeal like a robe.
notes: Or “righteousness” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NCV “goodness.”
Or “a breastplate” (traditional; so many English versions); TEV “a coat of armour.”
Heb “and [as] a helmet deliverance on his head.”
Heb “and he puts on the clothes of vengeance [as] a garment.”

verses.zh: 他必按人的行为施报，恼怒他的敌人，报复他的仇敌，向众海岛施行报应。
verses.en: He repays them for what they have done,dispensing angry judgment to his adversariesand punishing his enemies.[NOTE:1] He repays the coastlands.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in accordance with deeds, so he repays, anger to his adversaries, repayment to his enemies.”
Or “islands” (KJV, NIV).

verses.zh: 如此，人从日落之处必敬畏耶和华的名，从日出之地也必敬畏他的荣耀；因为仇敌好像急流的河水冲来，是耶和华之气所驱逐的。
verses.en: In the west, people respect[NOTE:1] the Lord’s reputation;[NOTE:2] in the east they recognize his splendor.[NOTE:3] For he comes like a rushing[NOTE:4] streamdriven on by wind sent from the Lord.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “fear.” A few medieval Hebrew mss read “see.”
Heb “and they fear from the west the name of the Lord.”
Heb “and from the rising of the sun his splendor.”
Heb “narrow”; NAB, NIV, NRSV “pent-up.”
Heb “the wind of the Lord drives it on.” The term רוּחַ (ruakh) could be translated “breath” here (see 30:28).

verses.zh: 必有一位救赎主来到锡安―雅各族中转离过犯的人那里。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “A protector[NOTE:1] comes to Zion,to those in Jacob who repent of their rebellious deeds,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: Or “redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
Heb “and to those who turn from rebellion in Jacob.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「至于我与他们所立的约乃是这样：我加给你的灵，传给你的话，必不离你的口，也不离你后裔与你后裔之后裔的口，从今直到永远；这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: “As for me, this is my promise to[NOTE:1] them,” says the Lord. “My Spirit, who is upon you, and my words, which I have placed in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth or from the mouths of your children and descendants from this time forward,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: The Lord promises the repentant (note “to them”) that they and their offspring will possess his spirit and function as his spokesmen. In this regard they follow in the footsteps of the Lord’s special servant. See 42:1; 49:2; 51:16. tn Or “my covenant with” (so many English versions); NCV “my agreement with.”
Heb “from now and on into the future.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- It is difficult to see how the different poems (i.e. chapters) relate in this section of Isaiah. I agree with
R. K. Harrison that Isaiah is an anthology of Isaiah's preaching/teaching/writing assembled after his
death. It is organized in an eastern way (thematic, word play) not a western chronological way.

- One wonders about these prophecies.

- Are they multiple fulfillment (i.e. Isa. 7:14; and Dan. 11:31; 12:11)?

- Do they express God's heart and desire for Israel, knowing that even with all the benefits
of covenant (cf. Rom. 9:4-5) they could not keep it (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27)?

- Are they poems/prophecies from different periods of Isaiah's ministry, addressing different
periods of Israel's history, but now arranged in a pattern that moderns do not comprehend? They
are given without historical setting and written in powerful Hebraic poetry. They could fit the
8thcentury, or the 7th, or the eschaton.

- Modern interpreters must remember

- this is poetry, not historical narrative (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY)

- these poems are presented without their specific historical setting (often Old Babylon and Neo-Babylon are not clearly differentiated)

- many of the words are used only once in the Bible or known Semitic literature (no cognate roots)

- Be careful of dogmatic doctrinal assertions from limited lines of poetry. Attempt to see

- parallelism

- parallel passages especially in Isaiah and Micah (8th century prophets)

- NT usage of the text/concept (cf. F. F. Bruce, Answers To Questions, pp. 87-88)

- The Jewish Study Bible (p. 901) sees this chapter in three parts.

- the prophet addresses the peoples' sin (i.e. corporately)

- the faithful in the nation acknowledge their sin (individually)

- the prophet announces YHWH's

- mercy to the faithful who repent (cf. Isa. 59:20,21)

- judgment to the hardened

(1) Jews

(2) the coastlands (i.e. Gentiles)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT:59:1-8

1Behold, the Lord's hand is not so short

That it cannot save;

Nor is His ear so dull

That it cannot hear.

2But your iniquities have made a separation between you

and your God,

And your sins have hidden His face from you so that He

does not hear.

3For your hands are defiled with blood

And your fingers with iniquity;

Your lips have spoken falsehood,

Your tongue mutters wickedness.

4No one sues righteously and no one pleads honestly.

They trust in confusion and speak lies;

They conceive mischief and bring forth iniquity.

5They hatch adders' eggs and weave the spider's web;

He who eats of their eggs dies,

And from that which is crushed a snake breaks forth.

6Their webs will not become clothing,

Nor will they cover themselves with their works;

Their works are works of iniquity,

And an act of violence is in their hands.

7Their feet run to evil,

And they hasten to shed innocent blood;

Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity,

Devastation and destruction are in their highways.

8They do not know the way of peace,

And there is no justice in their tracks;

They have made their paths crooked,

Whoever treads on them does not know peace.

59:1-2 These opening phrases clearly show the problem with God's promises to Israel; it was
not His word, character, or power but their repeated and continuing sin.

Verse 1 reflects the prophet's reaction to the questioning he hears from the Israelites
of his day (i.e. where are the Lord's promises?). Isaiah records the
murmurings of the people several times (i.e. Isa. 40:27; 49:4,14).

59:1 "hand" This is often a Hebrew idiom for activity (cf. Isa. 51:9). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

Notice the number of human body parts used to describe Deity (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN).

- hand

- ear

- face

Also notice how many human body parts describe human evil.

- hands, Isa. 59:3

- fingers, Isa. 59:3

- lips, Isa. 59:3

- tongue, Isa. 59:3

- feet alluded to in Isa. 59:7-8

▣ "save" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT).

▣ "dull" This word (BDB 457, KB 455, Qal PERFECT) means "to be
heavy," "to be burdensome," or "to be honored." In this context it refers to an inability to hear (cf. Isa. 6:9-10). It is used in
this same way as the "eyes" in Gen. 48:10 and of Pharaoh's "heart" in Exod. 9:7.

59:2 "iniquities" This term (BDB 730), from a root "to bend" or "to twist," is used of breaking God's laws.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2

▣ "made a separation between you and your God" The VERB (BDB 95, KB 110,
Hiphil PARTICIPLE) is used in several senses.

- God separating light from dark in Gen. 1:4

- God setting Israel apart from other peoples

- making a distinction between clean and unclean

- dividing into parts (i.e. sacrifices)

- YHWH and Moses setting apart Levites (especially Aaron, 1 Chr. 23:13)

- cutting off a person from Israel (cf. Deut. 29:20)

- excluding foreigners (cf. Neh. 13:3)

- setting apart musicians

- separating oneself from foreigners and pagans in one's society (cf. Ezra 6:21; 9:1; 10:11; Neh. 9:2)

- separating oneself to a specific leader (i.e. David, 1 Chr. 12:8)

In this context it is used in a unique sense. Israel's sins had emotionally and spiritually
separated the covenant people from the covenant God and His presence, promises, provisions, and protection!
The exile of the covenant people was not a sign of YHWH's weakness, but of their covenant disobedience!

One way to illustrate this terrible spiritual condition is the next parallel line of poetry. God hid
His face from them (i.e. He would not hear their prayers)! This is the opposite of Isa. 58:9.

59:3-8 These verses list (in parallel lines) the sins of Israel that had caused the separation (BDB 95).

- your hands are defiled with blood, Isa. 59:3

- your fingers defiled with iniquity, Isa. 59:3

- your lips have spoken falsehood, Isa. 59:3

- your tongue mutters wickedness, Isa. 59:3 (the VERB, BDB 211 I, is often connected to the
occult, cf. Isa. 8:19; 29:4; 47:12-13)

- courts are corrupt, Isa. 59:4 (notice the four INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES)

- you plan evil and violence, Isa. 59:5-7 (cf. Job 8:14-15; 15:35; Prov. 1:16; for Isa. 59:7 see Rom. 3:15-17)

- they did not know the way of peace (cf. Isa. 26:3,12; 57:20-21; Luke 1:79) or justice, Isa. 59:8 (notice
the four PERFECT VERBS)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

59:4 Verse 4, like Isa. 59:13, uses a series of INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES to describe evil human behavior.

- they trust in confusion, Qal. BDB 105, KB 120

- they speak lies, Piel, BDB 180, KB 210

- they conceive mischief, Qal, BDB 247, KB 255 (cf. Job 15:35)

- they bring forth iniquity, Hiphil BDB 408, KB 411

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT:59:9-20

9Therefore justice is far from us,

And righteousness does not overtake us;

We hope for light, but behold, darkness,

For brightness, but we walk in gloom.

10We grope along the wall like blind men,

We grope like those who have no eyes;

We stumble at midday as in the twilight,

Among those who are vigorous we are like dead men.

11All of us growl like bears,

And moan sadly like doves;

We hope for justice, but there is none,

For salvation, but it is far from us.

12For our transgressions are multiplied before You,

And our sins testify against us;

For our transgressions are with us,

And we know our iniquities:

13Transgressing and denying the Lord,

And turning away from our God,

Speaking oppression and revolt,

Conceiving in and uttering from the heart lying words.

14Justice is turned back,

And righteousness stands far away;

For truth has stumbled in the street,

And uprightness cannot enter.

15Yes, truth is lacking;

And he who turns aside from evil makes himself a prey.

Now the Lord saw,

And it was displeasing in His sight that there was no justice.

16And He saw that there was no man,

And was astonished that there was no one to intercede;

Then His own arm brought salvation to Him,

And His righteousness upheld Him.

17He put on righteousness like a breastplate,

And a helmet of salvation on His head;

And He put on garments of vengeance for clothing

And wrapped Himself with zeal as a mantle.

18According to their deeds, so He will repay,

Wrath to His adversaries, recompense to His enemies;

To the coastlands He will make recompense.

19So they will fear the name of the Lord from the west

And His glory from the rising of the sun,

For He will come like a rushing stream

Which the wind of the Lord drives.

20"A Redeemer will come to Zion,

And to those who turn from transgression in Jacob," declares the Lord.

59:9-11 These verses describe the results of Israel's sins (Isa. 59:3-8). This explains why YHWH's promises of
abundant restoration have been delayed.

- justice is far from us (see SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE)

- righteousness does not overtake us (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS)

- hope for light, but darkness comes (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT and SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS)

- hope for brightness but walk in gloom (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- grope along the wall like blind men (BDB 178, KB 206, Piel COHORTATIVE, twice,
cf. Deut. 28:29; Jer. 13:16; Amos 5:18,20; also note Isa. 6:9-10)

- growl like bears

- moan like doves

- hope for justice, but none comes

- hope for salvation but it is far away (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION [OT])

Number 6 is a metaphor, found only here in the OT. The TEV translates (paraphrases) it and
the next line as "we are frightened and distressed." The NASB Study Bible footnote characterizes it as
"impatient and frustrated."

Number 7's imagery is found in Isa. 38:14; Ezek. 7:16; and Nahum 2:7.

59:10d

NASB, NRSV
"among those who are vigorous"

NKJV, Rotherham
"in desolate places"

NJB
"among the robust"

REB
"in the desolate underworld"

JPSOA
"among the sturdy"

JPSOA footnote
"In the daytime"

LXX, Peshitta
"they will groan"

The MT has a PREPOSITION and the NOUN (BDB 1032, KB 96).
This root can mean

- robust, healthy

- fertile place

- among the stout (only here)

- desolate places (cf. Hosea 14:1 conjecture from BDB 79); KB 96 suggests "graveyard."

Obviously, the Hebrew is uncertain. JPSOA footnote emendation fits the parallelism of v. 10 best.

59:12 Verse 12 describes the current spiritual situation (cf. Isa. 1:2-4; 6:5).

- Israel's transgressions are multiplied before YHWH

- Israel's sins testify against them

- Israel's transgressions are present with them

- Israel knows her sins

Notice that Isaiah, like Ezra, confesses the corporate sin of the covenant people (cf. Ezra 9:6-7). This
is what the High Priest did on the Day of Atonement (cf. Leviticus 16). There is corporate guilt with consequences,
as there is individual sin and its consequences!

This may be a separate literary unit (TEV, NJB) which records the faithful remnants' confession of
sin. These repentant ones, and not all of Israel/Judah, are forgiven and restored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

59:13 Verse 13 describes the sins.

- transgressing ‒ BDB 833, KB 981, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- denying the Lord ‒ BDB 471, KB 469, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- turning away from God ‒ BDB 690, KB 744, Niphal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- speaking oppression and revolt ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- conceiving from the heart lying words ‒ BDB 247, KB 255, Poel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- speaking/uttering from the heart lying words ‒ BDB 211, KB 237, Poel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

Notice how the author artistically uses the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES in Isa. 59:4 and 13!
The faithless seed of Abraham show their true orientation (i.e. self) by their lifestyle (cf. Titus 1:16). They speak of
YHWH but live for self (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; 29:13; Matt. 7:15-29).

59:14-15a What are the results of these premeditated spiritual rebellions?

- justice is turned back

- righteousness stands far away

- truth stumbles in the street

- uprightness cannot enter

- truth is lacking

Notice the personifications! The one who tries to be righteous is a target and prey for the sinful!

59:15b-16b Israel, the covenant people, was YHWH's means of revealing Himself to the world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).
They had miserably failed. They, like all fallen humans, were incapable of following God.

- their actions and attitudes were displeasing

- there was no justice

- there was no righteous man

- there was no one to intercede (cf. Ezek. 22:30)

Therefore, YHWH must act Himself. This is similar theologically to Ezek. 36:22-36, which
describes the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34.

Notice that the prophet speaks about YHWH in Isa. 59:15b-20. YHWH speaks for Himself in Isa. 59:21.

59:16c-d In light of fallen humanity's (even covenant humanity) ability YHWH chooses to act.

- His own arm brought salvation to Him, cf. Isa. 52:10; 63:5

- His righteousness upheld Him

Who is the "Him"? In context it could be the Suffering Servant (i.e. Messiah) or YHWH's prophet (i.e. Isaiah).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUFFERING MESSIAH

59:17 YHWH is described as a "warrior" preparing for battle (i.e. the Divine Warrior, cf. Exod. 15:3; Josh. 5:13-15;
Ps. 24:8; Isa. 42:13; Rev. 19:11-16). This text is the OT background for Paul's use of this military imagery in Eph. 6:10-17
(see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRITUAL WARFARE).

- He puts on righteousness like a breastplate

- He puts on a helmet of salvation

- He puts on garments of vengeance

- He wrapped Himself with zeal as a mantle

59:18 "According to their deeds, so He will repay" This is a recurrent truth in Scripture
(cf. Job 34:11,25; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27;
25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).
All humans reap what they sow! There are consequences to choices and actions that follow
us through time. Thank God for divine forgiveness and forgetfulness!

Just an added thought; without choice, how can there be responsibility? Human choice can be clearly seen in

- YHWH forbiding eating of the tree of knowledge, Genesis 3

- YHWH's words to Cain in Gen. 4:7

- the call of Abraham, Gen. 12:1-3

- the consequences for blessing and cursing in Lev. 26; Deut. 28 (i.e. to the Mosaic covenant)

- the powerful call of Deut. 30:15,19 (i.e. "choose life")

These are just isolated, limited examples. How can humans be responsible for their actions, if all
is determined before by God's choices?

▣ "the coastlands" This word (BDB 15 I) is used often in this section of Isaiah
(cf. Isa. 40:15; 41:1,5; 42:4,10,12,15; 49:1; 51:5; 59:18; 60:9; 66:19) in the sense of other nations or Gentile nations.

59:19-20 The purpose of YHWH's recompense (BDB 168) is for redemption (i.e. fear the name of
the Lord). A Redeemer (cf. Isa. 41:14; 43:1; 44:22) comes from Israel (i.e. the
Messiah). He comes for all who "turn" (BDB 996, KB1427, Qal PARTICIPLE, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT]).

In the NT the context that struggles with Jewish unbelief and rebellion is Romans 9-11.
Paul uses Isa. 59:20 in Rom. 11:26-27. I think that Rom. 3:21-31; 9-10; Galatians 3; and the book of Hebrews
are the best NT texts to understand how the Old Covenant and New Covenant diverge and merge again!

For a good brief discussion of this text, please look at F. F. Bruce, Answers To Questions,
pp. 87-88. This is one of my favorite books!
